title: Meetings & Negotiations
completion_message: ¡Excelente! Con este vocabulario puedes liderar cualquier negociación, destrabar situaciones difíciles (deadlocks) y llegar a acuerdos beneficiosos.

parts.visual:
Términos Clave de Negociación: 
- Bargain (Negociar precio / Ganga). 
Ej: They bargained hard for a better deal. 
- Counter-offer (Contraoferta). 
Ej: We rejected their price and made a counter-offer. 
- Consensus (Consenso / Acuerdo general). 
Ej: We need to reach a consensus before the end of the meeting.
parts.audio: Key Negotiation Terms. 'Bargain' means to negotiate the terms of an agreement, usually price, or it can mean a good deal. For example: They bargained hard for a better deal. 'Counter-offer' is an offer made in response to another. For example: We rejected their price and made a counter-offer. 'Consensus' means a general agreement. For example: We need to reach a consensus before the end of the meeting.

parts.visual:
Resolución y Conflicto: 
- Deadlock (Punto muerto / Estancamiento). 
Ej: The negotiations have reached a deadlock. 
- Compromise (Ceder ambas partes para llegar a un acuerdo). 
Ej: We both want different things, so we will have to compromise. 
- Leverage (Poder de negociación / Ventaja). 
Ej: Since we have multiple suppliers, we have more leverage.
parts.audio: Resolution and Conflict. 'Deadlock' is a situation where no progress can be made. For example: The negotiations have reached a deadlock. 'Compromise' means an agreement where both sides make concessions. For example: We both want different things, so we will have to compromise. 'Leverage' is the power to influence a person or situation. For example: Since we have multiple suppliers, we have more leverage.

stages.title: Interactive Quiz
stages.description: Elige la palabra correcta para la situación de negociación.

questions.question: The negotiations have reached a ____. Neither side is willing to change their position. (Punto muerto).
To reach an agreement, both parties will have to ____. (Llegar a un acuerdo cediendo ambos).
questions.explanation: Compromise = compromiso donde ambas partes ceden en algo.

questions.question: They offered us $10,000, but we made a ____ of $15,000. (Contraoferta).
After hours of discussion, we finally reached a ____. Everyone agreed. (Consenso).
Because we are their only client, we have a lot of ____ in this negotiation. (Poder de negociación / Ventaja).
questions.explanation: Leverage = ventaja o poder de influencia en una negociación.

questions.question: You can try to ____ with the seller to get a lower price. (Regatear / Negociar).
I would like to propose a ____ situation where both companies benefit. (Ganar-ganar).
questions.explanation: Win-win situation = situación en la que todos ganan.

questions.question: Before the meeting starts, let's look at the ____. (Orden del día / Temas a tratar).
questions.explanation: Agenda = orden del día, lista de temas a discutir en una reunión.

questions.question: Who is going to take the ____ during this meeting? (Acta de la reunión / Notas).
questions.explanation: Take the minutes = levantar el acta de la reunión.

questions.question: We need to ____ the main points before we make a final decision. (Resumir).
Let's stick to the ____, please. We are getting off-topic. (Puntos de discusión).
questions.explanation: Stick to the agenda = ceñirse a los puntos de la reunión.

questions.question: The union is threatening to go on ____ if their demands are not met. (Huelga).
questions.explanation: Go on strike = ir a la huelga (contexto de negociación laboral).

questions.question: This is our ____ offer. We will not pay a single dollar more. (Oferta final/definitiva).
questions.explanation: Bottom-line offer (o simply 'final offer') = la oferta límite. 'The bottom line' también significa la conclusión o el resultado financiero final.

questions.question: If they don't accept our terms, we are prepared to ____ away from the deal. (Alejarse / Abandonar la negociación).
questions.explanation: Walk away = abandonar la negociación si no conviene.

questions.question: We had to make some ____ to keep the client happy. (Concesiones).
questions.explanation: Make concessions = hacer concesiones, ceder en ciertos puntos.

questions.question: The meeting was very ____. We solved all the issues in one hour. (Productiva).
Let's put that issue on ____ and discuss it later. (En espera).
questions.explanation: Put on hold = poner en espera, pausar.

questions.question: I would like to ____ a proposal regarding the new software. (Hacer/Presentar una propuesta).
questions.explanation: Make a proposal = hacer una propuesta.

questions.question: Could you please ____ what you mean by 'restructuring'? (Aclarar).
questions.explanation: Clarify = aclarar, explicar con más detalle.

questions.question: The two parties finally managed to ____ a deal. (Cerrar / Llegar a un acuerdo).
questions.explanation: Strike a deal = llegar a un acuerdo o trato.
